stem: A single drainage sample has much higher EC than the input solution. What is the strongest interpretation before changing irrigation or fertilizer settings?
choices: Treat the result as evidence of overfeeding and reduce fertilizer immediately, because drainage EC directly identifies excessive nutrient input and does not require comparison with moisture or recent trends
Treat the result as evidence the substrate became fully dry before irrigation, because high drainage EC is specific to severe dryback
Treat the result as evidence the input solution was mixed incorrectly, because drainage EC cannot exceed input EC under normal conditions
Treat it as one data point: verify sampling consistency and compare input EC, root-zone moisture, drainage behavior, and recent trends before assigning a cause
rationale: A single drainage EC result is not enough to identify cause. Interpretation should combine a verified sample with input conditions, root-zone water status, drainage behavior, and trend data before management changes are made.
